# c0mpute

> Decentralized compute marketplace. CLI-first. Pay workers with spare GPUs to run your jobs. Run your own GPU and earn. MIT-licensed, open source.

## Getting Started

- [Install](https://c0mpute.com/getting-started): One-line install via `curl -fsSL https://c0mpute.com/install.sh | sh`. Supports Linux and macOS (x86_64, aarch64).

## Run a node

- [Chat](https://c0mpute.com/chat): chat with open models served by c0mpute/Infernet provider nodes. Sign in with CoinPay (a CoinPay DID is required). Same chat from the CLI (`c0mpute chat login`, `c0mpute chat "prompt"`), an OpenAI-compatible API (base URL `https://c0mpute.com/v1`, `Authorization: Bearer c0k_...`), and MCP (`https://c0mpute.com/api/mcp`, tools chat, list_models, whoami; stdio via `c0mpute chat mcp`).
- [Chat prompt commands](https://c0mpute.com/docs#prompt-commands): a user message that starts with a registered slash command is expanded by the server into the command's instructions plus the question, on every surface (web chat, `c0mpute chat "/analyze ..."`, the TUI, `POST /v1/chat/completions`, the MCP `chat` tool). `/analyze <question>` answers data questions (understand, gather, analyze, validate, present). List: `GET https://c0mpute.com/api/v1/chat/commands` (public JSON). Commands are markdown files in the repo's `commands/` directory.
- [Agentic Advisor: Finance](https://c0mpute.com/advisor/finance): the finance pack of prompt commands: `/cashflow`, `/runway`, `/pnl`, `/spend`, `/forecast`, `/board <decision>` (hands figures to Board as a Service), plus `/analyze`. Data from the user's own Mercury, CoinPay or QuickBooks chat plugins (OAuth, read-only by default) or a pasted CSV; every answer ends "Analysis, not financial, tax or legal advice." Also on npm as `@profullstack/agentic-advisor-finance` (CLI + MCP server).
- [Chat API tool calling](https://c0mpute.com/docs#api): `POST https://c0mpute.com/v1/chat/completions` supports OpenAI tool calling: `tools` (function), `tool_choice` (auto/none/required/named), `parallel_tool_calls`, assistant `tool_calls` and `role: "tool"` results in history; replies carry `message.tool_calls` with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`, streamed as `delta.tool_calls`. Tool-capable models: qwen3:4b, nemotron-3-nano:4b, qwen2.5-coder:7b (tested), plus qwen3*, qwen3-coder, qwen2.5-coder:14b, qwen3.5 builds, devstral, llama3.1+, mistral-nemo; `model: "auto"` picks one; other models get a 400 rather than silently dropping tools. Also text content-part arrays (images 400) and `response_format` json_object. Two-step curl example in the docs.
- [Run a node](https://c0mpute.com/providers): `curl -fsSL https://c0mpute.com/install.sh | sh` installs c0mpute and starts the worker (Linux, macOS, Windows via WSL2; CPU or GPU). The goal is 100,000 nodes, enough pooled capacity to train and serve open-weight models in the open.
- [CPU and GPU earnings estimates](https://c0mpute.com/estimates): compare monthly scenarios at assumed paid utilization using live rental rates from r4ck.dev (median of current hourly GPU offers per card and VPS plans per CPU spec, refreshed daily, with a hand-checked fallback), next to observed c0mpute job prices over the last 7 and 30 days by hardware class and workload (agreed auction prices after the assumed fee, with sample size). Scenarios are not payout forecasts; observed prices are not settled payouts.
- [Market](https://c0mpute.com/market): GPU nodes online with each operator's listing. Fully competitive: every job is a sealed-bid auction under the buyer's cap and the lowest bid wins automatically; no rate card. New nodes default to a $0.001 minimum per job; existing node settings are preserved. `c0mpute pricing set --min <usd>` = dynamic pricing (starts at 60% of the cap, undercuts the winning price by 2% after a loss, probes up after a win, rises with queue load) never under the floor; 5% market fee on market jobs (the operator keeps 95%; Infernet charges the same 5% on paid inference and the two never stack); `--fixed <usd>` = one price. The listing (`pricing: {mode, min_usd, fixed_usd}`) is in https://c0mpute.com/api/nodes.
- [Node board](https://c0mpute.com/nodes): every node online now, ranked by `c0mpute bench` score, with the operator's nickname. JSON at https://c0mpute.com/api/nodes (`name` per node, `operators` = nodes online per nickname).
- Node nicknames: `c0mpute name <handle>` then restart the worker (`c0mpute worker stop && c0mpute worker start -d`), or install with `curl -fsSL https://c0mpute.com/install.sh | sh -s -- --name <handle>`. Stored in `~/.c0mpute/name`; `C0MPUTE_NAME` overrides it. Lowercase a-z, 0-9, - and _, up to 32 chars. Public and unverified; earnings follow the payout address, not the name. Needs 0.2.64+.
- [Leaderboard](https://c0mpute.com/leaderboard): anonymous top performers over 24h / 7d / 30d / all time: nodes (jobs served, bench score), operators by recorded earnings (real settled pay, never estimates), referrers, users, API (models, calls, tokens) and agents (MCP tool calls). Nobody is named: public node ids and `c0mpute name` nicknames as on /nodes, everyone else an `anon-xxxxxx` handle; boards with fewer than 3 people are withheld and customer spend is shown in ranges. JSON at https://c0mpute.com/api/leaderboard (rebuilt every 5 minutes). Opt out from the dashboard.
- [Benchmarks](https://c0mpute.com/benchmark): live CPU, cores, RAM, composite score and per-workload throughput for online nodes. These synthetic CPU workloads do not measure AI model inference speed.
- Referral links: https://c0mpute.com/r/<handle> gives an install line with `C0MPUTE_REF=<handle>`; nodes installed with it show the handle on the board. Public scoreboard, no payout.

## Docs

- [CLI Reference & Cookbook](https://c0mpute.com/docs): Full CLI walkthrough — identity/wallet, workers, transcode jobs, AI inference, reputation, plugins, health checks.

## Modules

- [Plugins](https://c0mpute.com/plugins): Three core modules — transcode (FFmpeg-based video encoding), coinpay (DID identity + escrow payments), infernet (AI LLM inference).

- [Blog](https://c0mpute.com/blog): Project updates and articles.
